comment: The ONE source of every recommendation LaneConductor makes (track AM-10128; track AM-10124's skill advisor, skill packs and third-party skills will add entries here, not text). scripts/plugin-texts.mjs generates from it: the Add-ons paragraph of the base SKILL.md, ADD-ONS.md, the fallback text of the board commands, the worktree pointer in run/implement/review, ops/board.md's 'missing' section and the README blocks. Fields: name (the plugin id); kind (addon | skillpack | thirdparty); display; source { marketplace: the marketplace name, add: what `claude plugin marketplace add` takes, plugin: the plugin id in it }; installs_code (true when the plugin ships a script or an MCP server: the generated note then says so plainly); installs (what it installs, one phrase, used when installs_code is true); why (one line: what it adds); adds (bullets); setup_fit (one line: the project facts that make it worth offering at setup; the setup step says 'It fits when ...' from it); detect (how Claude can tell it is installed); triggers (the only moments to mention it; a person asking, never a nag). connector/test/recommendations.test.mjs checks that every plugin named in the generated text is an entry here and that the install commands match .claude-plugin/marketplace.json. Never run an install: the commands are shown, the person runs them. `bundles` (AM-10128, owner decision 2026-11-18) names the plugins of the two one-line installs, in order; scripts/plugin-texts.mjs derives each line from these names and the marketplace in the entries, so no command is typed twice: full_install is for use OUTSIDE Claude (the website, the READMEs: the base and both add-ons), addons_install is for use INSIDE a Claude session where the base is already installed (both add-ons). A test checks that addons_install names exactly the kind addon entries.

entries.name: laneconductor-parallel
entries.installs: an MCP server (the connector, a Node.js program) and a scaffold script
entries.why: parallel work: isolated sub-agents, one per track in its own worktree, and safe shared state through conflict-checked track writes
adds: conflict-checked writes (a write is refused if someone edited first, so several sessions, people or sub-agents can write the same tracks at once)
automatic commits of the track changes it makes, and freshness warnings
a generated summary of all tracks
an advice log and a health report
a scaffold script for a new project
the `track-runner` sub-agent: one per track, each in its own git worktree
entries.setup_fit: the git history shows several authors, the project has CI files or several services, or the person wants tracks worked in parallel or by sub-agents
entries.detect: its connector tools exist (`mcp__plugin_laneconductor-parallel_lc__*`, for example `mcp__plugin_laneconductor-parallel_lc__get_track`), or its agent `laneconductor-parallel:track-runner` is listed
triggers: the person mentions several sessions, people or sub-agents writing the same tracks, or worries about overwrites
the person mentions worktrees or running tracks in parallel
the person asks for automatic commits, a privacy scan or a health report

entries.name: laneconductor-board
entries.installs: a script (a Node.js program, no packages) and its page
entries.why: the board, one private page of every track by lane, which Claude publishes as an artifact
adds: the script that builds the board page and data from the track files; Claude publishes them as a private artifact, only with the person's approval
it works with or without the other add-on
entries.setup_fit: a team will follow the tracks, the project already has more than a handful of them, or the person wants an overview of every track by lane
triggers: the person asks for a board or dashboard (`/laneconductor:board`, `/laneconductor:board refresh`)
